analysis.title: October 2026 Hedge Fund Recap
key_insights: The average Global L/S fund fell -3.1% in October vs MSCI AC World -1.6%. It was the 4th negative month of 2026 for Global L/S funds, after March (-4.6%), July (-1.8%) and September (-1.5%).
Global L/S alpha eroded on both sides of the book. Long alpha was -3.2% and short alpha -1.3% for the month. The YTD long-short spread is +1.8%, down from +7% through September.

Return dispersion is wide. The 25th percentile Global L/S fund is down ~4.1% YTD and about 40% of L/S funds are flat to negative YTD. The 90th percentile is up ~20.5% and the 10th percentile is down ~11.2%.
HFs were net sellers of global equities in October, mostly through long selling. Supply was led by N. America, then APAC, Japan and Europe. Multi-Strat/Macro and Equity L/S drove the net selling.

Equity L/S funds have actively unwound ~9% of global gross exposure since late June. This is the largest active L/S de-grossing across global equities in the last decade. Including price impact, it is smaller than the COVID drawdown (-30%) and the 2021-2022 period (~40%).
The global L/S ratio ex-quants is 1.86x, in the 3rd percentile over the last 12 months and the 1st percentile over the last 5 years.
US L/S funds cut N. America gross exposure by -6.6% since end of June. US L/S gross leverage ended October at 206% (3rd percentile on a 12-month basis). Net leverage is 47% vs a 53% YTD average.
US long alpha fell from ~10% YTD at its peak to +50bps YTD. Short alpha was negative in October.

MS notes that in prior mid-term election years HFs unwound gross exposure into the election and re-grossed afterward. The lack of a PnL cushion this year raises doubt that they will follow that pattern into year-end.

HF net exposure to AI themes fell from ~47% of US net exposure at end of June to under 35% in October. That is just under the ~36% AI weight in US equity market cap, the first underweight since the trade took hold. MS says this cuts both ways: HFs could sell further weakness or chase a rally.

HFs rotated out of Momentum, which fell -13.1% in October, and into Quality and Size by shorting low-quality and small-cap names. Russell 2000 short interest is above the 90th percentile across all three major HF cohorts. HFs began covering in the last ~7 sessions of October, but remain among the most bearish in a year.
The Quant and Multi-Manager median Global fund lost ~49bps in October (+89bps YTD, unlevered). Momentum cost -14bps and Beta ~4bps. Asia was the worst region at a median -96bps.

In Europe, the average EU-based HF fell -2.6% and the average EU-based L/S fund -2.5%, vs Euro STOXX 600 +2.0%. HFs kept trimming EU gross exposure even though EU net exposure is near 15Y+ lows and EU is under 15% of global gross.

The EU top-50 crowded long minus short spread fell -7.9% in October, the worst month in 10+ years and beyond July's -7.6% record. Both long and short alpha were negative, which has happened eight times since 2016, three of them in 2026.

In EU, longs were sold in oil majors and healthcare equipment. Tech hardware, miners and copper saw de-risking on both sides. Shorts were covered in EU AI disruption, software, high short interest and UK banks.

APAC saw the largest active L/S de-grossing in a decade, concentrated in AI longs across Taiwan, Japan and Korea. HF net exposure to Japan, Korea and Taiwan fell from ~23% to 15% of global net exposure. Asia Semis fell to 6% of global net exposure from a 13% peak in June.
Asia-based HFs lost -5.2% (L/S -4.9%) vs MSCI Asia Pacific -6.1%. APAC L/S top-50 spread fell -8% in October and is +7.2% YTD, down from ~27% at end of June.
By sector, Info Tech had the weakest L/S spread at -8.5% (longs ~-14%), though the YTD Tech spread is +13.0%. Materials was strongest at +2.0%, then Cons Staples at +1.5%.

sector_views.rationale: Tech longs fell ~14% in October, with the L/S spread at -8.5%. HF AI net exposure fell below its market cap weight for the first time. This describes hedge fund positioning, not a house sector rating.
Materials had the best October L/S spread at +2.0%, driven by shorts falling more than longs.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Global equities fell, and the average Global L/S fund fell more (-3.1%).
The average Americas-based L/S fund lagged at -2.6%.
EU-based HFs lagged despite the index rise, partly from US equity exposure.
Asia-based HFs lost less than the index.

risk_factors: Further weakness in crowded AI positions could force more HF selling, since AI is still a material share of portfolios and PnL.
A short squeeze in the Russell 2000, where HF short interest is above the 90th percentile.
HFs may not re-gross into year-end as mid-term election seasonality suggests, because there is no PnL cushion.
Crowded long and short alpha losses in Europe, where both sides of the book lost in the same month.
Further long selling in APAC AI names, where net exposure is already well below its peak.
vol_and_positioning: US L/S gross leverage is 206% (3rd percentile over 12 months) and net leverage is 47%.
Global L/S ratio ex-quants is 1.86x, in the 1st percentile over 5 years.

Russell 2000 short interest is above the 90th percentile across all three major HF cohorts. HFs covered shorts over the last ~7 October sessions but remain among the most bearish in a year, leaving the trade exposed to sharp moves higher.
HF AI net exposure is under 35% of US net exposure vs ~36% market cap weight. MS says HFs could sell more weakness or chase a rally.
HF net positioning to Momentum is at 12-month troughs, while Quality and Size tilts are near multi-year highs.
EU gross exposure is under 15% of global gross, the smallest share in over 15 years. EU net exposure is near 15Y+ lows.

tension_points.bull_case: HFs are now slightly underweight AI vs market cap (just under 35% of net vs ~36% of US market cap), so they would need to buy at a sharper clip to keep pace with a move higher.
tension_points.bear_case: AI names remain a material weight in portfolios and a key PnL driver, so HFs could be quick to sell into further weakness.

tension_points.bull_case: In prior mid-term election years HFs unwound gross into the election and added back afterward. US gross leverage is at 12-month troughs.
tension_points.bear_case: There is little PnL cushion, which calls into question whether HFs will deploy risk into year-end.

tension_points.bull_case: Short interest above the 90th percentile across all major HF cohorts leaves the trade open to sharp moves higher.
tension_points.bear_case: HFs remain among the most bearishly positioned in a year despite covering over the last ~7 sessions.
